INTRODUCTION

  • Social media has become one of the most influential communication platforms, where millions of users express their opinions, emotions, and feedback daily. Sentiment analysis — also known as opinion mining — is a natural language processing (NLP) technique used to identify and categorize opinions expressed in text to determine whether the sentiment is positive, negative, or neutral.

  • This project focuses on analyzing the sentiments of social media posts. By applying machine learning and NLP techniques, the aim is to automatically classify user-generated content and gain insights into public opinion trends. Such analysis can help businesses, researchers, and organizations understand customer satisfaction, brand perception, and emerging issues on social media.

ABOUT THE DATASET

  • The dataset used in this project contains textual data from social media posts along with their associated sentiment labels.

Typical columns include:

1.Text – the actual content of a user’s post.

2.Sentiment/Label – the sentiment class (e.g., Positive, Negative, or Neutral).

  • Before training, several data preprocessing steps were performed:

    1.Removal of unwanted characters, punctuation, URLs, and stopwords.

    2.Conversion of text to lowercase.

    3.Tokenization and lemmatization/stemming.

    4.Transformation into numerical format using TF-IDF or CountVectorizer.

COLUMN DESCRIPTION

Column Name Description
Year The year when the tweet was posted (e.g., 2018)..
Month The month of the tweet (numeric, e.g., 8 for August).
Day The day of the month the tweet was posted.
Time of Tweet Indicates the time of day when the tweet was made (e.g., “morning”, “afternoon”, “evening”, “night”).
Text The actual tweet or post content being analyzed.
Sentiment The sentiment classification of the tweet — likely one of “positive”, “negative”, or “neutral”.
Platform The social media platform where the post was made (e.g., “Twitter”).

def wordopt(text):
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"http\S+|www\S+|https\S+", '', text)  
    text = re.sub(r'\@w+|\#','', text)                 
    text = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z\s]', '', text)            
    text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()            
    return text
In [43]:
df['text'] = df['text'].apply(wordopt)
In [45]:
lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
In [47]:
def preprocess_text(text):
    words = word_tokenize(text)
    words = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(w) for w in words if w not in stop_words]
    return ' '.join(words)
In [51]:
df['text'] = df['text'].apply(preprocess_text)

CONCLUSION

  • This project successfully demonstrates how Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning can be applied to understand sentiments in social media posts. By converting unstructured textual data into meaningful insights, the system can automatically detect positive and negative emotions.

  • The trained model can be used for:

    1.Monitoring brand reputation,

    2.MultinomialNB is the best model of the project

    3.Analyzing social trends in real time.

  • Future improvements may include using deep learning models (e.g., LSTM, BERT) to handle context more accurately and enhance prediction performance.
